disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Regulations for season dates, structures, and restrictions were adopted by the F&W Commission on Aug. 19, 2026 and are valid through June 30, 2027; the Commission reserves the authority to amend them. Quota-driven early closures apply — always verify current quota status and regulations with FWP before trapping.

license_summary.trapping_license: General Trapper License: resident $20, available to resident conservation license holders 12+. Nonresident Trapper License: $250 (issued through FWP offices). Landowner Trapper: $1 resident. Youth Trapper (ages 6-11): free resident license, valid for mink and muskrat only. All licenses must be purchased by Nov. 30 each year to be valid for bobcat.
license_summary.wolf_license: Wolf License: $12 resident / $50 nonresident; must be purchased by Feb. 28, 2027. Maximum of 10 per person. Class C or C-2 wolf trapping license for trappers. Completion of the Idaho or Montana wolf trapping certification class is mandatory to trap wolves.
license_summary.trapper_education: Trapper education is required for any resident trapper who has not purchased a trapping license for three years in their lifetime (not necessarily consecutive); does not apply to those trapping for livestock or property protection.
license_summary.harvest_reporting: Harvest of bobcat, otter, swift fox, fisher, wolf, and marten must be called in within 24 hours (1-877-FWP-WILD). Pelts must be inspected and tagged within 10 days of the calendar close of the season at an FWP office. All wolf skulls and hides must be presented UNFROZEN within 10 days of harvest for tagging, tissue sampling, and tooth extraction.
license_summary.quota_closure: In districts with quotas, seasons close with 48 hours notice upon reaching or approaching the quota (24-hour notice for wolf), or on the season closure date, whichever is first. Current status: 1-800-711-8727 or 406-444-9557, 24 hours a day; or fwp.mt.gov.
license_summary.nonresident_bobcat: Nonresidents may not hunt or chase bobcats.
license_summary.supplemental_permit: A free Supplemental Trapping Permit is required for all trappers (except those using water sets or live cage traps) inside the geographic scope identified by federal court order when targeting nongame (raccoon, badger, red fox) and predatory animals (coyote, striped/striped skunk, spotted skunk, weasel).
license_summary.state_land: A Special Recreational Use License for Trapping (SRULT) from DNRC is required before trapping on state trust land for persons 12 and older.
license_summary.wma_regulations: State Wildlife Management Areas have specific closures and season dates (e.g., Lake Helena WMA drawing, Freezout Lake WMA units, Haggin WMA). See WMA Special Regulations in the booklet.

Modeled as continuous open since no season dates are printed.
